html:
A Zarma teacher who led Niger to independence from France on 3 August 1960 and was its president until 15 April 1974.

His Nigerien Progressive Party ruled as the only party, and he banned the rival Sawaba movement and put down its armed attempt in 1964. He kept close ties to France and was a respected mediator in African diplomacy. He negotiated hard with France over the price of uranium from Arlit. The great Sahel drought and famine of the early 1970s, and charges of corruption around him and his wife, led to his overthrow by Seyni Kountche. His wife was killed in the coup.
sum: A Zarma teacher who led Niger to independence from France on 3 August 1960 and was its president until 15 April 1974.
